meta.gift: longing, tide of the blood, and light gentle enough to lie by
meta.waning: the shards drift apart; nights arrive unscheduled and grief acquires weight
meta.curse_desc: moonlight pools in the eyes of the afflicted, who weep light until none is left to see by
veils: The shards the churches keep are not relics but ransoms, paid to keep the nights scheduled.
The gentle light was never the Moon's — it is borrowed, and the lender has begun to collect.
The Moon broke itself to hide the lender's name among its shards; assembled, they would speak it, and the debt would come due all at once.
meta.epigraph: Of the Sundered Moon little now is spoken, and less is true. Gather what the old things still remember, and be sparing with belief.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the Sundered Moon gave the world longing, tide of the blood, and light gentle enough to lie by.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The gods withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter. Then the waning began: the shards drift apart; nights arrive unscheduled and grief acquires weight.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. The gods are silent, the roads belong to the marked, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the Sundered Moon rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world longing, tide of the blood, and light gentle enough to lie by.

e2.text: Galomere, god of graves and the ledger of names, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e3.text: Ysirveth, god of harvest, plenty, and the debt of plenty, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: Yoryne, god of war and the keeping of thresholds, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e5.text: Quelmund, god of healing and the price of healing, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e7.text: The Mirror of Galomere was wrought as regalia of Galomere's throne.

e9.text: The Shard of Ysirveth was wrought as regalia of Ysirveth's throne.

e11.text: The Mirror of Yoryne was wrought as regalia of Yoryne's throne.

e13.text: The Veil of Quelmund was wrought as regalia of Quelmund's throne.

e14.text: Nimgrim, the Unreflected, rose against the thrones. Quelmund led the gods to war.
e14.hidden: Ysirveth treated with Nimgrim in secret and was spared what followed.

e15.text: Nimgrim was defeated and sealed beneath Nimenmothreach; the seal was bought with the lives of 9 champions.

e16.text: The waning began: the shards drift apart; nights arrive unscheduled and grief acquires weight. Mortals called the affliction the Silver Lament: moonlight pools in the eyes of the afflicted, who weep light until none is left to see by.

e17.text: Yseric the Adamant founded the Order of the Veil at Toriagrimbarrow, sworn to stand against the Silver Lament.

e18.text: The Church of Yoryne was raised at Velothasmere; Solendra of the Long Vigil took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e19.text: Velaeeth the Lantern-eyed was cast out of Church of Yoryne and founded the Cult of the True Shard, teaching that the gods themselves caused the waning.
e19.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e20.text: Nyessorn the Lantern-eyed united the river-clans and was crowned in Hestvethshroud; the realm took the name Belthashollow.

e21.text: At the urging of Solendra, the saint Serdis the Kindly was given to the Sundered Moon in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e21.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Solendra suspected as much.

e22.text: Harach the Kindly, sword-hand of Nyessorn, opened the gates of Hestvethshroud to the Order of the Veil over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e22.hidden: Harach acted on a promise from the Cult of the True Shard: that the marked of their house would be spared the Silver Lament. The promise was not kept.

e23.text: Belthashollow fell. Nyessorn the Lantern-eyed died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e24.text: Harach was found at Veranynereach bearing the Silver Lament, and was not spared.

e25.text: Ysirveth, god of harvest, plenty, and the debt of plenty, took the Silver Lament — the first of the gods to bear it — and wandered from their seat.
e25.hidden: The curse does not distinguish gods from mortals. It never did.

e26.text: Kamoth the Unmarked, last-sworn of the Order of the Veil, set out for the place where Ysirveth was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.

e27.text: Kamoth returned once, said nothing, left their sword upon the order's altar, and walked into the dusk unarmed.

e28.text: Pilgrims of the Cult of the True Shard were found digging at the seal of Nimgrim. The wardens hanged nine; the digging continued.
e28.hidden: The seal has been failing on its own since the waning began. The cult only follows the cracks.

Of the champions spent on the seal, most are a list now; two are still prayed to by name — Soldis the Younger and Olott of the Rearguard — though none can say what distinguishes the remembered dead from the rest. The tellings differ, but most agree a wardenship was sworn over the seal, hereditary and unthanked. Its rolls have never once been complete. Whether this was mercy or malice, none agree.
